subject: Ingress strategy decision: PrivateLink vs peering vs site-to-site for AcmeAnalytics
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <networking@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ingress strategy decision: PrivateLink vs peering vs site-to-site for AcmeAnalytics

Samir —

Thanks for taking the time to review connectivity options with us. Attached are two artifacts to ground the discussion: a short comparison matrix (redwood-privatelink-vs-peering-matrix.xlsx) and a sketch of a proposed topology (acme-topology-proposal-20270629.png).

High level options we typically evaluate:
- VPC Peering: lowest latency, simplest for high-throughput internal traffic, but requires large-scale CIDR planning and may not be allowed for some compliance profiles.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): strong security model (no cross-VPC routing), good for controlled API access; tradeoffs are per-endpoint ENI and potential egress/az charges and slightly higher latency than peering.
- Site-to-Site VPN / Transit: flexible, can traverse your on-prem network or firewall appliances; generally higher and less predictable latency, and more operational overhead to maintain.

For this thread please share the following so we can converge on a recommendation and PoC scope:
1) Any policy blockers for VPC peering (procurement/infra/security).
2) Expected sustained and peak API requests/sec and average payload size (tokens/MB).
3) Whether control-plane telemetry (metrics/traces) must transit the same path as inference traffic.
4) Preferred cloud region and whether you want cross-region failover.

Initial thought from our side: if compliance allows peering, it gives the best latency for high-throughput inference. If not, PrivateLink + a small edge aggregator for bulk uploads (sits in your VPC) is a reasonable hybrid to balance cost and privacy. If you have large model artifacts or heavy telemetry that must remain on-prem, pair PrivateLink with a site-to-site encrypted tunnel for artifact syncs.

We can present cost/latency numbers in the next call — Ben and Monica will run modelling. Can you confirm whether your network team prefers an endpoint-based model (PrivateLink) or a routed model (peering/VPN)?

Thanks,
David

Subject: Re: Ingress strategy decision: PrivateLink vs peering vs site-to-site for AcmeAnalytics

David —

Appreciate the clear comparison and the diagram. A few constraints from our side:
- Compliance: our security policy (internal) strongly prefers not to allow any broad peering that exposes internal CIDR ranges. Peering would need a formal exception and a justification to legal.
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~350 requests/sec to the Redwood inference endpoint, with occasional spikes to 1500 rps (short bursts, 30–60s). Typical payloads are small (avg ~1.2 KB per request).
- Egress: we are sensitive to cross-AZ charges and want to understand per-token/GB egress cost differentials.
- Firewall/NVA: traffic must pass through our perimeter firewall for inspection; any solution that requires additional publicly routable endpoints will need explicit approval.

Given the policy, PrivateLink looks attractive because it limits the surface area — but we’re worried about ENI limits and the operational complexity of managing many interface endpoints if we go multi-region.

We are happy to run a PoC. Suggested next steps:
- PoC scope focused on API calls only (no model artifact syncs initially).
- Attempt PrivateLink in us-west-2 with a single endpoint; measure p50/p95 latency and per-hour cost.
- If latency/cost are unacceptable, discuss a limited peering exception for a read-only peering route to the inference subnet only.

Who should I loop in from our cloud infra team? I can add our cloud network lead (Rajesh Kumar) if that helps.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Ingress strategy decision: PrivateLink vs peering vs site-to-site for AcmeAnalytics

All —

Based on Samir's constraints (+ the traffic profile), here's a practical, differentiated recommendation that keeps security owners happy while optimizing cost/latency: a staged hybrid PoC. Key points: 

1) Stage 1 — PrivateLink-only (PoC):
   - Single interface endpoint in us-west-2 for inference API. Limits surface area and avoids CIDR exposure.
   - Deploy a lightweight aggregator (edge proxy) in Acme's VPC (single t3.medium or managed Fargate) to batch internal telemetry and act as a NAT/eBPF-based connection manager. This reduces the number of ENIs and avoids per-VM endpoint sprawl.
   - Measure p50/p95 latency for small payloads, token throughput, and per-hour endpoint cost.

2) Stage 2 — Conditional peering for high-throughput bulk path:
   - If PrivateLink p95 latency or egress cost is consistently >20% worse than our peering baseline or if spikes cause throttling, apply for a scoped peering exception limited to a single CIDR and a dedicated inference subnet.
   - Peering only for model artifact syncs / bulk telemetry, with strict route table controls and no general-purpose route propagation.

3) Fallback — Encrypted S2S tunnel:
   - If your compliance/security team requires inspection through on-prem appliances, we can terminate a dedicated IPsec session to your firewall for artifact syncs. Latency will be higher — use for non-latency-sensitive data only.

Operational considerations and estimates: 
- ENI limits: our edge-aggregator pattern reduces per-VM ENI usage. We'll provide a script to estimate the number of endpoints and ENIs per AZ.
- Costs: For initial sizing (350 rps steady, 1500 rps bursts) we expect PrivateLink to cost roughly 10–25% more than peering for pure egress bytes but to be competitive when you factor in the operational overhead and security exceptions required for peering. We'll produce a short cost model before the PoC call.
- Monitoring: We recommend enabling token-level logging to a constrained telemetry bucket (short retention) and routing traces over the same endpoint.

I'll prepare the cost/latency model and a short runbook for the PoC. Proposed timeline: kickoff this week, 3-day PoC, decision meeting at the end of week.

Ben

1) Kickoff call Thursday 11:00am PT — 30 minutes (PoC scope, roles, tentative cutover plan).
2) Ben will share a short cost/latency model by EOD today.
3) We'll provision a single PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2 and provide a small terraform snippet and runbook for your infra team (includes ENI estimate and security group recommendations).

Action items for you: please invite Rajesh Kumar (cloud network lead) and confirm whether the perimeter firewall will allow connections to interface ENIs in our account (we can provide the destination IP ranges).

If the PoC shows acceptable latency and per-hour cost, we can keep the PrivateLink approach. If not, we'll present a scoped peering design that limits CIDR exposure and route propagation.

I'll send a calendar invite and the PoC runbook shortly. Looking forward to the call.
